_note: The dense map. Twenty by twenty like West Bambulon and nothing like it: forty of its four hundred tiles carry a place or something to read, which is the Look Outside register written down as a budget a test can check. Most of the readables sit off the roads on purpose — a card that opens every time you cross the field is a card a player learns to shut without reading. The Drambus Stack is four tiles of `curd` in the middle, which is its own terrain because a two-hundred-and-ten-foot cheese drawn as rock is a hill. Its door is written as an event and not a gate: the floors behind it are M11.3's, and a gate onto a map this build has not got is a hole where a promise should be. The two pools are ordered on purpose: `draw_enemy` weights a pool so its hardest member is its rarest, so the creature an errand asks for is the *easiest* thing in its region and never the hardest. Getting that backwards is `PLAN.md` §6b row 1 written into content — a set behind the rarest creature, one map further out. **The shadow was retuned down in M11.3.** At a mean of eight hundred it was a gauntlet you crossed to reach the tower and then crossed again after every floor, and a walk that had to cross it six times lost eighteen hundred fights doing it. The hard part of a tower should be the tower. **A fourth creature joined the shadow in M11.7**, and the reason is the weighting rather than the danger: `draw_enemy` makes the hardest member the rarest, so Bone Cantor at the top of three was one draw in five hundred and the living earth off it was seven hundred and fifty wins. Crowned Hollow stands above it now and the earth is seventeen. `PLAN.md` §6b row 1, paid a third time.

places.name: the road down to the Treyway
the way into the Drambus Stack
places.shut: There is a stump where the door was, eleven inches of rind and a frame lying flat in it with the hinges still on, and a board propped against it with five strokes chalked on and all five rubbed out.
prose: The frame has closed round the door by an inch on every side and the door opens anyway, inwards, on hinges nobody has oiled since the works stopped putting a year on things.

Inside is a floor. Not a room and not a stair — a floor, two hundred feet across, with the ceiling four feet above your head and something at the far end of it that has been waiting long enough to have stopped pacing.

places.name: the cart, by the quench pond
prose: A cart with one wheel chocked and a canvas over it, and a person sitting on the tailgate with a ledger they are not reading.
Everything on it is somebody else's survey, sold by weight. They will not say whose and they will not be here on Thursday.

_caravan: **Eight stops and the cart is at one of them.** A place that moves cannot be a place spawned at runtime — *places are content and content is not state* — so every stop it makes is authored here on empty walkable ground, and `WorldState::caravan` says which one has the cart on it today. `place_is_there` hides the other seven. Five of your steps on this field and it goes somewhere else, never to the stop it is already at and never onto the tile you are standing on.
